q: 1. The maximum bending moment due to a moving load on a fixed ended beam occurs
explain: For a fixed-ended beam under a moving load, the greatest bending moment magnitude generally develops at the fixed supports due to the restraining moments there.

q: 2. In which of the following truss members, the stress depends upon, whether the load is moving on top chord or bottom chord
explain: In a truss, diagonal members' force sign and magnitude depend on which chord (top or bottom) the moving load acts on, unlike the chords or verticals which react more consistently.

q: 3. A two hinged semi circular arch of radius R carries a concentrated load W at the crown. The horizontal thrust is
explain: Standard analysis of a two-hinged semicircular arch with a central point load at the crown gives a horizontal thrust of H = W/π.

q: 4. The analysis of structure is
options: deciding the material of the member
deciding the dimension of the member
calculating the magnitude and nature of various straining actions at salient points of the structure
explain: Structural analysis is the process of determining the internal forces (straining actions) like shear, moment, and thrust at critical points, not deciding material or dimensions (which is design).

q: 5. In a two hinged arch, an increase in temperature includes
options: no bending moment in the arch rib
uniform bending moment in the arch rib
maximum bending moment at the crown
minimum bending moment at the crown
explain: A rise in temperature in a two-hinged arch causes the arch to expand against its fixed horizontal thrust, inducing a uniform bending moment throughout the arch rib.

q: 6. If there m unknown member forces, r unknown reaction components and j number of joints then degree of static indeterminacy of a pin jointed plane frame is given by
explain: For a pin-jointed plane frame, the degree of static indeterminacy is Ds = m + r − 2j, since each joint provides 2 equilibrium equations (ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0).

q: 7. Number of unknown internal forces in each member of a rigid jointed plane frame is
explain: In a rigid-jointed plane frame member, there are three internal force components at each cross-section: axial force, shear force, and bending moment.

q: 8. Independent displacement components at each joint of a rigid jointed plane frame are
options: two linear movements and one rotation
one linear movement and two rotations
explain: A rigid joint in a plane frame can translate in two directions (x, y) and rotate about one axis (z), giving 2 linear movements and 1 rotation as independent displacement components.

q: 9. Find the bending moment at fixed end for the structure as shown in fig.
explain: The bending moment at the base is calculated by the horizontal force multiplied by the vertical lever arm (10T × 2m = 20 Tm).

q: 10. For a two hinged arch, if one of the support settles down vertically, then the horizontal thrust
explain: A vertical settlement of one support in a two-hinged arch reduces the rise, thereby reducing the induced horizontal thrust.

q: 11. For a beam having fixed ends, the unknown element of the reactions, is
options: horizontal component at one end and vertical component at the other
horizontal and vertical components at both the ends
explain: A fixed support can resist horizontal force, vertical force, and moment; for a beam fixed at both ends, unknown reactions include horizontal and vertical components (plus moments) at both ends.

q: 12. A column is aid to be of medium size if its slenderness ratio is between
explain: By common classification, columns with slenderness ratio between about 32 and 120 are treated as medium/intermediate columns.

q: 13. Columns of given length, cross-section and material have different values of buckling loads for different end conditions. The strongest column is one whose
options: one end is fixed and other end is hinged
both ends are hinged or pin jointed
one end is fixed and the other end entirely free
explain: A column fixed at both ends has the smallest effective length (Le=L/2), giving the highest Euler buckling load, making it the strongest configuration.

q: 14. The rise of a parabolic arch at quarter points, is equal to
options: 1/3 times the rise of the crown
1/4 times the rise of the crown
1/2 times the rise of the crown
3/4 times the rise of the crown
explain: For a parabolic arch, using y = 4hx(l−x)/l², at quarter span (x=l/4) the rise works out to (3/4) of the central rise h.

q: 15. In a three hinged arch, the shear force is usually
explain: In a three-hinged arch, shear force is typically maximum near the springing (supports) where the arch's slope relative to loads is greatest.

q: 16. The equations of compatibility are written based on
options: the geometry of the deformed structure under the action of several forces acting
explain: Compatibility equations ensure that the deformed shape of the structure is geometrically continuous and consistent with the supports.

q: 17. An internally indeterminate structure
options: may be an unstable structure based on supports
explain: Internal indeterminacy refers to the redundancy of internal members. Per the provided key, it is categorized here as being associated with an externally determinate setup.

q: 18. A sinking prop is one which
options: does not permit any deflection at all
is provided below the level of regular supports and becomes effective after the respective deflection occurs
explain: A sinking prop refers to a support that undergoes a predetermined settlement or only engages once the structure has deflected to a certain point.

q: 19. A suspension cable, supporting loads will be under
explain: A flexible suspension cable can only carry axial tension (it cannot resist bending or compression), so it is always under pure tension.

q: 20. A three hinged girder is used to stiffen a cable of a suspension bridge. Then the bending moment in the girder due to loads will be
explain: In an ideal stiffened suspension system with a three-hinged girder matching the cable's thrust line, the girder carries zero bending moment throughout, all load being carried by cable tension.

q: 21. Which of the following structural analysis is a force method?
explain: Column analogy treats the redundants as forces, making it a force-based method.

q: 22. Stiffness factor is calculated in structural members for analyzing it by
explain: The moment distribution method relies heavily on member stiffness to distribute unbalanced moments.

q: 23. The stiffness method in structural analysis is also known as :
explain: The stiffness method uses displacements as the primary unknowns, hence it is a displacement method.

q: 24. The equations of compatibility are based on
options: the geometry of the deformed structure under the action of several forces acting
explain: Compatibility equations ensure that displacements/deformations throughout a structure remain geometrically consistent (continuous) under the applied loading.

q: 25. A concentrated load P is supported by the free end of a quadrantal ring AB whose end B is fixed. The ratio of the vertical to horizontal deflections of the end A is
explain: For a quadrant ring under an end load, applying Castigliano's theorem to find vertical and horizontal deflection components gives a ratio of π/2.

q: 26. The moment required to rotate the near end of a prismatic beam through a unit angle without translation, the far end being simply supported is given by
explain: The rotational stiffness of a prismatic member with the far end simply supported (pinned) is 3EI/L, a standard slope-deflection method coefficient.

q: 27. The degree of kinematic indeterminacy of a pin jointed space frame is
explain: Each joint of a pin-jointed space frame has 3 possible translational displacements, so kinematic indeterminacy = 3j − r (subtracting restrained reaction components).

q: 28. The number of independent displacement components at each joint of a rigid jointed space frame is
explain: A rigid joint in 3D space can have 3 translations and 3 rotations, giving 6 independent displacement components per joint.

q: 29. A bar l meter long and having its area of cross section A, is subjected to a gradually applied load W. the strain energy stored in the bar is
explain: Strain energy stored in a bar under a gradually applied axial load W is U = W²L/2AE, the standard formula (area under the linear load-deformation curve).

q: 30. Which of the following is a relatively ductile material?
explain: Mild steel, with its low carbon content, exhibits significant ductility (large elongation before failure) compared to the more brittle options listed.

q: 31. In the simultaneous equations derived from slope deflection method, the matrix formed by the coefficients of various rotations will have
options: all elements along the diagonal zero
diagonal symmetry with diagonal element predominant in that respective equation
explain: The stiffness matrix from slope-deflection equations is symmetric, with diagonal (self-stiffness) terms typically dominant compared to off-diagonal (coupling) terms.

q: 32. The elements of flexibility matrix of a structure
options: are dependent on the choice of co ordinates
are independent of the choice of co ordinates
explain: The flexibility matrix elements are defined relative to a chosen set of coordinates (degrees of freedom) for the structure, so they depend on that choice.

q: 33. Which of the following methods of structural analysis is a force methods?
explain: The column analogy method is a force (flexibility-based) method of structural analysis, unlike slope deflection and moment distribution which are displacement methods.

q: 34. In the displacement method of structural analysis, the basic unknowns are
explain: In displacement (stiffness) methods, the primary unknowns solved for are the joint displacements (translations and rotations).

q: 35. The width of the analogous column in the method of column analogy is
explain: In column analogy, the 'width' (intensity) of the analogous column load/section corresponds to 1/EI, representing the M/EI diagram's scaling.

q: 36. The moment distribution method is formulated by
explain: The moment distribution method was developed by Hardy Cross.

q: 37. The maximum deflection of a fixed beam carrying a central point load lies at
explain: By symmetry, for a fixed beam under a central point load, the maximum deflection occurs exactly at the midspan (centre) of the beam.
